title: Fitting a two-port zone valve to a heating circuit
subtitle: Install a motorised zone valve on a wet central heating or hot water circuit for independent zone control
excerpt: How to fit a two-port motorised zone valve to a wet heating circuit. Covers isolating the circuit, fitting the valve body in the correct flow direction, connecting the wiring to the wiring centre, and commissioning the controls.
sourceNotes: Collins Complete DIY Manual (referenced, not reproduced). UK central heating controls trade practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: A motorised valve with one inlet and one outlet that opens or closes a heating circuit under the control of a thermostat. When the thermostat calls for heat, the motor opens the valve and an end switch in the valve sends a signal to the boiler and pump to run. UK standard zone valve sizes are 22 mm (heating circuits) and 15 mm (smaller domestic hot water diverter applications). Honeywell V4043 and Drayton LE4 are common UK types.

A terminal strip box that centralises all the low-voltage control wiring connections for a central heating system: thermostats, zone valves, programmer, boiler, and pump. The wiring centre is the hub that enforces the correct control sequence (zone valve calls for heat, end switch fires boiler and pump). Located near the boiler or consumer unit.

Step 1: Isolate, drain, and cut in the valve position

Close the isolation valves either side of the planned valve position and drain the pipework between them by releasing a drain cock or opening the lowest draw-off point on the circuit. Cut a 120 mm section of pipe to create the gap for the zone valve body (check the installed face-to-face dimension from the valve datasheet). Fit the valve body using compression fittings either side, with the flow arrow on the valve body matching the direction of water flow.
Step 2: Isolate the electrical supply before wiring

attrs.title: Mains voltage at the wiring centre
attrs.body: The wiring centre carries 230 V mains terminals. Isolate the circuit breaker or fused spur feeding the boiler and controls before opening the wiring centre. Use the two-pole voltage tester with the proving unit to confirm the terminals are dead before connecting any wires.

content.text: Run the 5-core cable from the zone valve actuator head to the wiring centre. Connect the five conductors (grey, orange, white, blue, and earth) following the wiring diagram for the specific valve type (Honeywell, Drayton, or Grundfos diagrams are available in the installation instructions). Typically: blue to neutral, grey to switched live from the zone thermostat, white to boiler/pump live, orange to permanent live via a fuse, and earth to earth.

Clip the motor assembly onto the valve body. Restore the water supply and check the compression joints for leaks. Restore the electrical supply. Test the zone valve by calling for heat from the zone thermostat: the valve should open (listen for the quiet motor sound) and the boiler and pump should fire. Use the manual override lever on the valve head to open the valve without power as a further commissioning check.

attrs.symptom: Boiler fires but the zone does not heat up
attrs.cause: Valve opens but the end switch wiring is incorrect, so the boiler fires but the pump does not run.
attrs.fix: Re-check the white wire (pump/boiler live) connection at the wiring centre. The valve end switch must have a complete circuit to activate the pump.

attrs.symptom: Valve leaks at the compression fitting after installation
attrs.cause: Olive not fully seated on the pipe, or olive was over-compressed during fitting.
attrs.fix: Close the isolation valves, loosen the compression nut, inspect the olive (replace if deformed), and re-tighten to two flats past hand-tight.
